'''Disasters and accidents''' 
*[[2024 Pakistan heat wave]]
**At least 568 people have died from heat-related illnesses due to extreme temperatures and humidity in southern [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/climate-change/news/pakistan-karachi-heatwave-temperature-death-toll-b2569734.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn05rz3w4x1o (BBC News)]
*[[2024 Sudan famine]]
**An [[Integrated Food Security Phase Classification]] (IPC) report states that over 755,000 people in [[Sudan]] face the most severe IPC level of extreme hunger as well as the worst levels of acute food insecurity ever recorded in the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/27/over-750000-people-in-sudan-at-risk-of-starvation-global-hunger-monitor (Al Jazeera)]
*Seven people are killed and five others are injured when a train collides with a bus near [[Nové Zámky]], [[Slovakia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/slovakia-train-bus-collision-nove-zamky-52d79ef77f0c9982120336a6ceb6574c (AP)]
*Three people are killed and 40 others are injured in a [[Derailment|train derailment]] amid heavy rains in [[Komi Republic|Komi]], [[Russia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-train-derailment-3a3613774af9221dcbcb2f7fd503ab67 (AP)]
*The [[Russia]]n satellite [[Resurs-P No.1]] breaks up into over 100 pieces of debris near the [[International Space Station]]. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/space/russian-satellite-blasts-debris-space-forces-iss-astronauts-shelter-2024-06-27/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Foreign involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***According to an anonymous [[South Korea|South Korean]] government official, [[North Korea]] is preparing to send [[Korean People's Army|engineering forces]] to the Russian-occupied [[Donetsk Oblast|Donetsk region]] of Ukraine in July. [https://www.nknews.org/2024/06/fact-check-north-korea-has-not-announced-plans-to-send-troops-to-ukraine-yet (NK News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Abortion in the United States]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States|US Supreme Court]] issues a ruling in ''[[Moyle v. United States]]'', dismissing the case and reinstating the ability to perform exceptional emergency abortion care in [[Idaho]], where a [[Abortion in Idaho|formal ban on abortion]] is in place. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/06/27/us/politics/supreme-court-idaho-abortion.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://idahocapitalsun.com/2024/06/28/u-s-supreme-court-ruling-reinstates-ability-to-perform-emergency-abortions-in-idaho-under-ban/ (''Idaho Capital Sun'')]
*[[Opioid epidemic in the United States]]
**In ''[[Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P.]]'', the [[Supreme Court of the United States|United States Supreme Court]] blocks a proposed [[Purdue Pharma]] bankruptcy settlement that would have shielded members of the [[Sackler family]] from civil lawsuits relating to the [[opioid epidemic]], citing issues regarding the protection of third parties from lawsuits. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/06/27/politics/purdue-pharma-supreme-court-opioid-settlement/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party]] expels former [[Minister of National Defense (China)|defense ministers]] [[Li Shangfu]] and [[Wei Fenghe]] from the [[Chinese Communist Party|party]] following charges of [[Corruption in China|corruption]] against them. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/china-former-defence-minister-li-shangfu-expelled-communist-party-4439876 (CNA)]
*[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] signs a law establishing [[English language|English]] as an official language of international communication in [[Ukraine]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/zelensky-signs-law-on-use-of-english-in-ukraine/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')]
*The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] charges 193 people, including 76 medical professionals, with participating in healthcare [[fraud]] schemes totalling $2.75 billion, which include unlawful distribution of [[Adderall]] and fraudulent drug addiction treatment. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/us-justice-department-charges-193-defendants-275-billion-health-care-fraud-bust-2024-06-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 United States presidential debates]]
**The first [[United States presidential debates|U.S. presidential debate]] for the [[2024 United States presidential election|upcoming presidential election]] is [[2024 Joe Biden–Donald Trump presidential debate|held]] between incumbent [[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]] and former president [[Donald Trump]] on [[CNN]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/first-presidential-debate-2024-trump-biden/ (CBS News)]
*[[Kenya Finance Bill protests]]
**Thousands of people protest in cities across [[Kenya]], calling for the removal of [[President of Kenya|President]] [[William Ruto]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/27/kenya-protesters-call-for-president-rutos-removal-after-tax-bill-dropped (Al Jazeera)]
*The leaders of the [[European Union]] member states agree to nominate [[Ursula von der Leyen]] as [[President of the European Commission]] and [[Estonian Prime Minister]] [[Kaja Kallas]] as the next [[High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy]], and elect former [[Portuguese Prime Minister]] [[António Costa]] as the next [[President of the European Council]]. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2024/06/27/eu-leaders-agree-on-top-jobs-ursula-von-der-leyen-antonio-costa-and-kaja-kallas (Euronews)]
